notes: The ledger's '~77,000 · 5.7 per 100,000' does not appear anywhere in the WHO report as read; the report prints the African Region at 66 000 deaths (22% of global drowning deaths) and 5.6 per 100 000 population for 2021, in Section 1 text and Fig. 2 'Number and rate of drowning deaths by WHO region' on printed page 14. WHO's own 13 December 2024 news release independently states 5.6 per 100 000 for the African Region. The Fig. 2 caption itself does not print a year; the surrounding Section 1 text frames the estimates as 2021, and the figure's source line reads 'Source: (3)' (the fetch tool reported reference (3) as WHO Global Health Estimates; a reviewer should confirm in the reference list). Values in Fig. 2 are rounded as printed. Other values read from the same figure, not added as rows because they are outside this task: global 300 000 deaths, 3.8 per 100 000; Western Pacific 84 000 (28%), 4.3; South-East Asia 83 000 (28%), 4.0; Eastern Mediterranean 35 000 (12%), 4.4; Americas 17 000 (6%), 1.6; European 15 000 (5%), 1.7. Section 1 (printed pp. 17-18) gives the 2000-2021 rate change for the African Region as a 3% fall. Caveat on provenance: WHO's IRIS server refused every fetch, so the report was read from a mirror copy of the PDF hosted by Spain's Ministry of Health; the document's title page and ISBNs (978-92-4-010396-2 electronic, 978-92-4-010397-9 print) matched, but a reviewer should spot-check page 14 against WHO's own copy when reachable. The origin of the old 77,000 / 5.7 figure was not identified. The row's numeric low/high/unit/year fields were not shown to this task, so no correction is proposed for them; the reviewer may wish to set deaths 66000 and rate 5.6 with year 2021.
